Rashi on Pesachim 69b:10:1.english: And [it is] necessary - for Rav to teach us [that] the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Akiva in both [cases].

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:10:2.hebrew: מילה - שלש עשרה בריתות נאמר בה, באותה פרשה שנאמרה לאברהם (בראשית יז):
Rashi on Pesachim 69b:10:2.english: Circumcision - Thirteen covenants are stated regarding it, in that section that was spoken to Abraham (Genesis 17).

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:11:1.hebrew: דליכא כרת - לבו ביום, אם ימול למחר:
Rashi on Pesachim 69b:11:1.english: As there is no karet - on that very day, if he circumcises [him] tomorrow.

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:12:1.english: When do they bring a Festival peace-offering with it - In the Gemara, it asks: what did [the Tanna] teach earlier, that it teaches [about] a Festival peace-offering?

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:12:2.hebrew: עמו - עם הפסח בארבעה עשר בניסן, כדיליף בגמרא:
Rashi on Pesachim 69b:12:2.english: With it - With the Paschal offering on the fourteenth of Nisan, as [is] derived in the Gemara.

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:12:3.hebrew: בזמן שבא בחול ובטהרה - דאף על גב דפסח דחי שבת וטומאה, חגיגה לא דחיא שבת:
Rashi on Pesachim 69b:12:3.english: When it comes on a weekday and in [a state of] ritual purity - For even though the Paschal lamb overrides Shabbat and ritual impurity, the Festival peace-offering does not override Shabbat.

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:12:4.hebrew: ובמועט - שהיה הפסח מועט לאכילת בני החבורה, ואוכלין החגיגה תחלה, כדי שיהא פסח גמר שביעתן ותיחשב להן אכילה:
Rashi on Pesachim 69b:12:4.english: And in a small [amount] - [Meaning] that the Paschal offering was too small for the members of the group to eat, so they eat the Festival peace-offering first, in order that the Paschal offering be the completion of their satiety and be considered [a satisfying] eating for them.

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:12:5.english: In abundance - [Meaning] that the group was small, and the Paschal lamb alone is sufficient for them.

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:13:1.hebrew: מן הצאן ומן הבקר כו' - מה שאין כן בפסח, שאינו בא מן הבקר ולא מן הנקבות:
Rashi on Pesachim 69b:13:1.english: From the flock and from the herd, etc. - Which is not the case with the Paschal offering, as it does not come from the herd nor from females.

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:14:1.hebrew: תנא הרכבתו כו' - וקאמר נמי בהך סיפא: אימתי מביאין כו', ואשמעינן דחגיגה נמי לא דחיא שבת, אפילו שחיטה דילה:
Rashi on Pesachim 69b:14:1.english: It taught its carrying, etc. - And it also states in this latter clause, "When do they bring, etc.," and teaches us that the Festival peace-offering also does not override Shabbat, even its slaughter.

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:1:1.hebrew: וכל שביחיד נדחה - והכי פירושא: היינו טעמא דר' אליעזר, לא רמיא חיובא דפסח אטמא מת בשביעי שלו הואיל ולא חזי, ואערל רמיא חיובא ואע"ג דלא חזי. ומשום דלא דמיא מצות הזאה למצות מילה, דמצות הזאה כדי לעשות פסח לא רמיא אציבור, שהרי מותרין לעשות בטומאה אע"פ שיכולין ליטהר. דקסבר רבי אליעזר אין שוחטין וזורקין על יחיד טמא שרץ שלא טבל, ואף על פי שראוי לערב, וכן על טמא מת שחל שביעי שלו להיות בערב הפסח, שראוי נמי לערב. וטמא שרץ נקט משום דפלוגתא גביה הוא בפ' האשה (דף צ:). וכיון דקא סבר אין שוחטין וזורקין על היחיד אלא נדחה לשני, על כרחיך ציבור עושין בטומאה אם ירצו, דכל שביחיד נדחה ציבור עושין בטומאה, דכתיב "איש איש" — נדחה, ואין ציבור נדחין. אלמא לא רמיא מצות הזאה דפסח אציבור, ומילתא דליתיה בציבור ליתיה ביחיד, דמצות פסח יחד לכל ישראל נאמר. אבל ערילות, דלא נדחה אצל ציבור ולא הותרו לעשות פסח ערלים, ואילו כולהו ציבור ערלים אמרי' להו "קומו מהולו" — יחיד נמי אמרינן ליה בחול "קום מהול". והזאה, דציבור לא אמרי' להו "קומו אזו":
Rashi on Pesachim 69b:1:1.english: And whatever in an individual is deferred - And this is its explanation: This is Rabbi Eliezer's reason [why] the obligation of the Pesach [offering] does not rest upon one who is impure from a corpse on his seventh [day], since he is not fit [to partake of it], whereas upon an uncircumcised person the obligation does rest even though he is not fit. And [this is] because the mitzvah of sprinkling is not comparable to the mitzvah of circumcision, for the mitzvah of sprinkling in order to offer the Pesach [sacrifice] does not rest upon the community, since they are permitted to offer [it] in [a state of] impurity even though they are able to become pure. For Rabbi Eliezer holds [that] we do not slaughter [the Pesach offering] and sprinkle [its blood] on behalf of an individual who is impure from a creeping creature [and] who has not immersed, even though he is fit [to partake of it] in the evening, and similarly on behalf of one who is impure from a corpse whose seventh [day] falls on the eve of Pesach, who is also fit in the evening. And he mentioned one who is impure from a creeping creature because the dispute regarding it is in Chapter HaIsha (90b). And since he holds [that] we do not slaughter and sprinkle on behalf of the individual, rather he is deferred to the second [Pesach], perforce the community offers [it] in impurity if they wish, for whatever is deferred in [the case of] an individual, the community offers in impurity, as it is written, "any man" — [an individual] is deferred, but a community is not deferred. Thus, the mitzvah of sprinkling for Pesach does not rest upon the community, and anything that does not apply to the community does not apply to an individual, for the mitzvah of Pesach was stated for all of Israel together. However, [regarding] uncircumcision, which is not deferred for a community — for uncircumcised [people] are not permitted to offer the Pesach, and if the entire community were uncircumcised we would say to them, "Arise, circumcise yourselves!" — to an individual as well we say on a weekday, "Arise, circumcise yourself!" Whereas [regarding] sprinkling, where to the community we do not say, "Arise, sprinkle!" [it does not apply to an individual either].

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:2:1.hebrew: יחיד נמי - לא רמיא חובה עלויה להזות, וכיון דלא רמיא עליה, לא ניתנה שבת לדחות אצלה. אבל אי הוה סבירא ליה כמאן דאמר שוחטין וזורקין על טמא שרץ, כיון דלא קרינא ביה "איש נדחה", לא הוה קרינא נמי "אין ציבור נידחין" למישרינהו לעשות בטומאה, אלא אמרינן להו: קומו אזו. ומדרמי' הזאה אציבור, הוה רמיא נמי איחיד כדי להתירו באכילה, ודחיא שבת:
Rashi on Pesachim 69b:2:1.english: An individual, as well - No obligation rests upon him to be sprinkled [with purifying water]; and since [the obligation] does not rest upon him, Shabbat was not given to be overridden for it. However, if [Rabbi Eliezer] had held like the one who says [that] one slaughters [the Paschal lamb] and sprinkles [its blood] on behalf of one who is impure from a creeping creature, since we would not apply to him [the rule that] "an individual is deferred" [to the second Pesach], we would also not apply [the rule that] "a community is not deferred" so as to permit them to perform [the offering] in a state of impurity; rather, we would say to them: "Arise, sprinkle [yourselves]!" And since sprinkling would rest upon the community, it would also rest upon an individual in order to permit him to eat [the Paschal lamb], and [thus] it would override Shabbat.

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:4:1.hebrew: אמר ליה - התם, האי דאיתיה ביחיד, משום דעבוד ציבור בראשון הוא. ואי לא עבוד ציבור בראשון, כגון רוב ציבור זבין — דלא הותרה טומאת זיבה בציבור — ומיעוטן טמאי מתים, אין עושין לא את הראשון ולא את השני:
Rashi on Pesachim 69b:4:1.english: He said to him - There, the reason that it applies to an individual is because the community offered [the Paschal lamb] on the first [Pesach]. But if the community did not offer [it] on the first [Pesach] — for example, [where] the majority of the community are zavim, as the impurity of zivah was not permitted for the community, and a minority of them are impure from a corpse — they offer neither the first nor the second.

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:5:1.hebrew: ערל וטמא שרץ ושאר - הדומין לו, כגון כל טמאי טומאת ערב שראויין ליתקן, וכגון טמא מת שחל שביעי שלו בערב הפסח:
Rashi on Pesachim 69b:5:1.english: Uncircumcised, or impure from a creeping animal, and the others - [That is,] those similar to him, such as all those impure with an evening impurity who are able to be rectified [through immersion], and such as one impure from a corpse whose seventh [day] falls on the eve of Passover.

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:6:1.hebrew: מדקא מיהדר אטמא שרץ - לאיתויי מקרא יתירא, שמע מינה סבירא ליה להאי תנא: אין שוחטין וזורקין על טמא שרץ. דאי סבירא ליה שוחטין וזורקין עליו, למה לי לאהדורי עליה מקרא יתירא לחיוביה? ממילא הוא עומד בכרת, שהרי הוא כטהור גמור, שראוי לעשות פסחו על ידי שליח לשולחו בעזרה, דכי פטר קרא מכרת, הנך דלא יכלו לעשות פסח פטר. אלא ודאי, אין שוחטין וזורקין עליו סבירא ליה, ואפילו הכי מיחייב ליה כרת, משום דיכול לטבול וליתקן משהגיע זמן שחיטה. ואף על גב דציבור כי האי גוונא לא אמרינן להו "זילו טבולו", דכיון דיחיד נדחה — ציבור עבדי בטומאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 69b:6:1.english: From the fact that he searches for one who is ritually impure from a creeping animal - [searching] to include [him] from an extra verse, infer from this that this Tanna holds: one may not slaughter [the Paschal lamb] and sprinkle [its blood] for one who is ritually impure from a creeping animal. For if he held [that] one may slaughter and sprinkle for him, why would I need to search for an extra verse for him to obligate him? Automatically he stands [liable] to karet, for behold, he is like one who is completely pure, since he is fit to have his Paschal offering made through an agent to send it into the Temple Courtyard, as when the verse exempts from karet, it exempts those who were unable to make the Paschal offering. Rather, certainly he holds [that] one may not slaughter and sprinkle for him, and even so he is liable to karet, because he is able to immerse and become fit once the time of slaughter has arrived. And even though for a community in such a case we do not say to them, "Go and immerse," for since an individual is deferred [to the Second Pesach], a community performs [it] in a state of impurity.

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:7:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא - אי הוה סבירא ליה אין שוחטין, דמעכבא ליה הזאתו משחיטת פסחו, ודאי דחיא שבת לר' אליעזר, אע"ג דליתא בציבור. אלא קסבר שוחטין וזורקין, הלכך הזאה למאי אתיא? לאכילה, דהא לא מיעכבא לה לשחיטה ולזריקה:
Rashi on Pesachim 69b:7:1.english: Rather, Rava said - If he held [that] we do not slaughter, such that his sprinkling prevents him from slaughtering his Paschal offering, it would certainly override Shabbat according to Rabbi Eliezer, even though it does not apply to the community. Rather, he holds [that] we slaughter and sprinkle; therefore, for what [purpose] does the sprinkling come? For eating, since it does not prevent the slaughtering and the sprinkling.

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:7:2.hebrew: אכילת פסחים לא מיעכבא - והא דכתיב (שמות י״ב:ד׳) איש לפי אכלו, למצוה:
Rashi on Pesachim 69b:7:2.english: Eating of the Paschal offerings is not essential - And that which is written (Exodus 12:4), "each man according to his eating," [is only] for a mitzvah [i.e., not indispensable].

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:8:1.hebrew: אם כן - דטמא מת שחל שביעי שלו בערב הפסח בשבת, שוחטין וזורקין עליו, ואע"פ שאין סופו להזות היום:
Rashi on Pesachim 69b:8:1.english: If so - that [for] one who is ritually impure from a corpse whose seventh [day] falls on the eve of Passover on Shabbat, they slaughter [the Paschal lamb] and sprinkle [its blood] on his behalf, even though he will not be sprinkled [with purification water] today.

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:8:2.hebrew: נמצא פסח זה נשחט שלא לאוכליו - ותנן באידך פירקא (לעיל פסחים דף סא.), שחטו שלא לאוכליו, פסול:
Rashi on Pesachim 69b:8:2.english: It turns out that this Paschal lamb is slaughtered for those who cannot eat it - And we learned in the other chapter (above, Pesachim 61a): "[If] one slaughtered it for those who cannot eat it, it is disqualified."

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:9:1.hebrew: כלל א"ר עקיבא כל מלאכה שאפשר לעשותה מערב שבת - כגון הבאתו מחוץ לתחום וחתיכת יבלתו:
Rashi on Pesachim 69b:9:1.english: Rabbi Akiva stated a principle: Any labor that can be performed on the eve of Shabbat - Such as bringing it [the Paschal lamb] from outside the [Shabbat] boundary and cutting off its wart.

Rashi on Pesachim 69b:9:2.english: And we also learned - regarding circumcision.

Tosafot on Pesachim 69b:10:1.hebrew: וצריכא דאי אשמעינן כו' - אדרב יהודה עביד צריכותא, אמאי איצטריך למיפסק בתרוייהו כר"ע; דאי אדר' עקיבא, הוה ליה לאצרוכי ההיא דפרק שתי הלחם (מנחות דף צו.) גבי חביתי כהן גדול, דמסיק התם: "כלל א"ר עקיבא כו'":
Tosafot on Pesachim 69b:10:1.english: "And it is necessary, for had [Rav] taught us, etc." - [The Gemara] is making a tzerikhuta [explanation of necessity] regarding Rav Yehudah['s ruling], [explaining] why it was necessary to rule in accordance with Rabbi Akiva in both [cases]. For if [the tzerikhuta were] regarding Rabbi Akiva [himself], it would have had to include that [case] in the chapter Shtei HaLechem (Menachot 96a) regarding the griddle-cakes of the High Priest, where it concludes there: "Rabbi Akiva stated a general rule, etc."

Tosafot on Pesachim 69b:10:2.hebrew: אבל מילה שנכרתו עליה י"ג בריתות אימא דנידחי - תימה: מה מועיל מה שנכרתו עליה י"ג בריתות? הא איכא קרא באפי נפשיה למכשירין, כדפי' לעיל. ונראה לרשב"א לפרש, דאי לאו דפסק רב יהודה כר"ע גבי מילה, ה"א דסבירא ליה בכל מקום כר' אליעזר, וגבי פסח דפסק כר"ע — היינו להחמיר מדרבנן, שלא יהו מכשירין דוחין שבת; אבל גבי מילה, דנכרתו עליה י"ג בריתות, לא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 69b:10:2.english: "But [regarding] circumcision, upon which thirteen covenants were established, I would say that it should override [Shabbat]" - This is astonishing: what does it help that thirteen covenants were established upon it? Behold, there is an independent verse for [its] facilitators, as explained above! And it appears to the Rashba to explain that had Rav Yehudah not ruled in accordance with Rabbi Akiva regarding circumcision, I would have thought that he holds in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer in every place, and regarding the Paschal lamb, where he ruled in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, that was [only] to be stringent by rabbinic decree, so that facilitators would not override Shabbat; but regarding circumcision, upon which thirteen covenants were established, [the Rabbis did] not [decree stringently].

Tosafot on Pesachim 69b:6:1.hebrew: מדקמהדר אטמא שרץ קסבר אין שוחטין כו' - מכל מקום חייב הוא כרת, לפי שהיה יכול לטבול, ואז היו שוחטין וזורקין עליו, כדאמר לקמן: "שוחטין וזורקין על טבול יום, דשימשא ממילא ערבא":
Tosafot on Pesachim 69b:6:1.english: From [the fact] that he searches for one who is impure from a creeping animal, he holds [that] one may not slaughter, etc. - Nevertheless, he is liable [to receive] karet, because he could have immersed [in a mikveh], and then they would have slaughtered and sprinkled [the blood] for him, as [the Gemara] states later: "One may slaughter and sprinkle for a tevul yom [one who immersed that day], for the sun sets on its own."

Tosafot on Pesachim 69b:7:1.hebrew: אכילת פסחים לא מעכבא - פי': בכי האי גוונא שיש בידו לתקן עצמו ואינו מתקן, לא מעכבא, אבל בטמא גמור מעכבא, דהוי דומיא דחולה וזקן. ולא כפירוש הקונטרס, דפי' דהא דכתיב "איש לפי אכלו" היינו למצוה; דהא לעיל (פסחים דף סא.) אוקימנא ליה לעכב, ומסיק בכיצד צולין (דף עח:) מ"איש לפי אכלו" דבעי' גברא דחזי לאכילה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 69b:7:1.english: Eating of the Paschal offerings is not essential - Explanation: In a case such as this, where it is in his power to rectify himself [and become pure] and he does not rectify [himself], it is not essential; however, for one who is completely impure, it is essential, for he is comparable to a sick person and an elderly person. And [this is] not like the explanation of Rashi, who explained that that which is written, "each man according to his eating" [Exodus 12:4], is [only] for a mitzvah [i.e., optimal fulfillment]; for earlier (Pesachim 61a) we established it as essential, and [the Gemara] concludes in [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin (78b) from "each man according to his eating" that we require a person who is fit for eating.

Tosafot on Pesachim 69b:8:1.hebrew: האי מיחזא חזי ותקוני הוא דלא איתקן - הקשה ריב"א: א"כ, אמאי אמר ר"א לעיל "ערל שלא מל ענוש כרת"? הא מיחזא חזי, אלא דלא איתקן! וי"ל דשאני התם, דמחוסר מעשה בגופו, וחשבינן ליה שלא לאוכליו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 69b:8:1.english: "This [person] is fit, and it is [only] that he has not been made ready" - Riva asked: If so, why did Rabbi Eliezer say above, "An uncircumcised [male] who did not circumcise [himself] is liable to karet"? Surely he is fit, [and] only that he has not been made ready! And it can be answered that it is different there, because he lacks an act upon his own body, and [therefore] we consider him among those who cannot eat it.

Tosafot on Pesachim 69b:9:1.hebrew: הלכה כר"ע - הא דלא פריך "הלכתא למשיחא", מפורש [בפ' ד' מיתות סנהדרין] (דף נא:):
Tosafot on Pesachim 69b:9:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Akiva - [The reason] that [the Gemara] does not ask, "[Is this] a halakha for the Messianic era?" is explained [in the chapter Arba Mitot, Sanhedrin] (51b):
